clue.text: And, shortly before turning 50, Madonna's disputed strip?

parts.note: 'n' is a shortened and, as in rock 'n' roll

indicators.note: turning means the gathered letters are spun round into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
the singer's name with its possessive S, all used as letters

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about the pop singer approaching her fiftieth birthday and something contested.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'disputed strip' is the ground between two front lines that neither side owns. 'turning' scrambles N, L and MADONNAS together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names land between opposing armies or claimants, a contested strip belonging to nobody.

clue.text: Treetop bats round lake practise thought transference?

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the next piece
bats means crazy, so the letters of treetop are jumbled

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: An odd picture of bats around a lake in the treetops attempting telepathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' rearranges TREETOP and 'round' wraps those letters about L.
explanation.definitionFit: In science fiction, beaming people across space is a kind of transfer, here whimsically extended to thoughts.

clue.text: Happy? Shame — that's arrogant

parts.note: to be up is to be cheerful or in good spirits
'what a shame' and 'what a pity' mean the same

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being happy is a shame, then dismisses that attitude as conceited.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone self-important who acts above their station.

clue.text: Small carnivore shortened portico

indicators.note: shortened means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the stoat is a small meat-eating mammal of the weasel family

explanation.surface: A small predator with a docked tail beside a colonnade.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade in ancient Greek architecture, essentially a portico.

clue.text: Drama when non-permanent male employee is included in trial

indicators.note: is included in means the first pieces are placed inside the next

parts.note: a test is a trial
a male temporary worker could be called a he-temp: HE for male, TEMP for a non-permanent employee

explanation.surface: A theatrical tale of a temporary male worker being put on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is included in' puts HE plus TEMP inside TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late play about Prospero is a celebrated drama.

clue.text: Hardly celebs, "X" and "Y"?

definitions.meaning: people nobody has heard of are the opposite of celebrities
in algebra, x and y stand for quantities yet to be found

explanation.definitionFit: Obscure people and algebraic variables are both things not yet known, giving the plural noun two senses.

clue.text: Not the feature film villain's footwear?

parts.note: a B-movie was the supporting picture shown before the main feature
a rogue is a scoundrel or villain

explanation.surface: A question about the shoes worn by the bad guy in a supporting picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinemas once showed a cheap B-film before the main feature, so 'not the feature film' gives B.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a sturdy leather shoe with decorative perforations, an item of footwear.

clue.text: Go before it and be lost

definitions.text: Go before it and be lost

parts.words: Go before it and be lost
parts.note: put the word go in front of a compass direction and the idiom means to perish or be lost

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'go west' means to die or be lost, so the compass point fits after go.

clue.text: Bowl a full toss — it's ended on asphalt!

parts.note: something over has finished or ended
pitch is a tarry substance like asphalt

explanation.surface: A cricket complaint that a bowler's delivery finished up on the tarmac.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ball pitched too far up, so it reaches the batsman without bouncing, is a full toss.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket term for bowling a ball too far up towards the batsman, so it arrives as a full toss.

clue.text: Stupid reason to lose one's tongue

indicators.note: stupid suggests letters thrown together without sense, an anagram

parts.note: taken as written for the letter pool
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A silly excuse for someone to fall silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' tells you to remove A from REASON; 'Stupid' then rearranges the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means a language, and this is the old Scandinavian language of the Vikings.

clue.text: Maybe Morecambe's bounded by a mother country

indicators.note: bounded by means the first piece is enclosed by the others

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, so his first name is a Morecambe

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a seaside town is surrounded by a motherland.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is also a Lancashire seaside town, which the surface uses; ERIC Morecambe was half of TV comedy duo Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is commonly called by this name, a country.

clue.text: Mean to hold on when the next dark time comes

definitions.text: when the next dark time comes

indicators.note: to hold means the first word contains the next

parts.note: tight means stingy or mean with money

explanation.surface: Someone stingy hangs on until nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means this coming evening or night, the next spell of darkness.

clue.text: Account level in the US

definitions.meaning: a tale or narrative is an account
Americans spell the floor of a building without the E used in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a narrative and the American spelling of a building floor.

clue.text: Certain amount of friction casually reported in an unspecified place

parts.note: some means a certain amount

indicators.note: reported signals a word heard rather than seen, said casually

parts.note: wear is damage caused by friction

explanation.surface: A loose report about how much rubbing happened, location unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at some place that is not named or known.

clue.text: Drink and jam gets journalist censored

parts.note: to sup is to drink
to press is to squeeze or jam
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer gets drink and jam, then has his story cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Something censored has been kept from publication, held down by authority.

clue.text: What's wrong with ensign wrapping up well?

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: the word what, its 's being is and a link

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is the matter with a flag being bundled up.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap in bandages or cloth, and the prefix intensifies the wrapping.

clue.text: A name current crowd associates with social beings: "spirit raisers"

parts.note: a tide is a current of water
a press is a dense crowd
ants live in highly organised colonies

explanation.surface: A rambling statement linking crowds and sociable creatures to things that lift the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: These medicines treat depression, raising a sufferer's spirits.

clue.text: Finished going round river track somewhere in France

indicators.note: going round means the first word encircles the others

parts.note: done means finished
to dog someone is to track them

explanation.surface: A completed journey around a river trail in rural France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'track' is a verb here, to follow someone; 'going round' signals the container. The Dordogne is a region of south-west France popular with British visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: This department and river region in south-western France is indeed a place there.

clue.text: It makes Art roar out after bank's No 3 teller

indicators.note: after means the anagram follows the bank letter
No 3 picks the third letter of the word
out signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that makes art roar, working at a bank's third counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teller' looks like a bank clerk, matching 'bank' in the surface, but it means a storyteller. 'out' signals the anagram; 'after' places it behind the bank letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A teller is one who tells a story, as a storyteller tells a tale.

clue.text: Leave salt over old soldier

parts.note: to desert is to leave

indicators.note: over means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a salt and a tar are both old words for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor abandoned by an old veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: The Desert Rats were British soldiers of the 7th Armoured Division in North Africa, now old veterans.

clue.text: Predators showing quiet craft

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
arks are boats or craft

explanation.surface: Predatory creatures display silent cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: These ocean fish hunt other creatures, so they are predators.

clue.text: Name state with retro look

parts.note: MA is the postal abbreviation for Massachusetts

indicators.note: retro means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: Naming a state with a vintage appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, an example of a name.

clue.text: Fictional detective's temperature dropped, denoting a fast day

indicators.note: dropped means a letter is removed from the name

parts.note: Maigret is Simenon's fictional Paris police inspector

explanation.surface: A famous fictional sleuth loses his body heat on a day of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Catholic calendar the term describes a day when meat is not eaten, a fast day.

clue.text: Jack gets each soul turning green

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

indicators.note: turning means the letters of soul are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jack gets every soul feeling sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Green with envy is the idiom; green means envious.

clue.text: Sooty's spouts

parts.note: jet is a black mineral, so jet-black is sooty
the clitic 's is taken as an S

explanation.surface: Something sooty has its own spouts.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Sooty's' as JET plus S: jet black is as dark as soot.
explanation.definitionFit: Spouts of water or gas are jets.

clue.text: Canny source of strength for the pipe-smoking sailor

definitions.text: Canny source of strength for the pipe-smoking sailor

parts.words: Canny source of strength for the pipe-smoking sailor
parts.note: a cartoon sailor with a pipe squeezes vegetables from a tin to gain huge strength; canny means coming in a can, not shrewd

explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon sailor eats this tinned leafy vegetable for instant strength.

clue.text: Boastful manner of resident rid of split lease

indicators.note: rid of means letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: rent is a lease payment, here split so its letters come from both ends

explanation.surface: A tenant who breaks a lease is accused of showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: RE and NT are taken from the two ends of RESIDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for pretentiousness or putting on airs.

clue.text: Mark, Barbie's friend, toasted so?

parts.note: when raising a glass we say 'to' followed by the name
Ken is the companion doll of Barbie

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark, a friend of Barbie, is the subject of a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a sign or mark of something.

clue.text: Cover for the sleeping seabird (blue)

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck
feeling down means feeling blue

explanation.surface: A bedcover for a melancholy seabird at rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt filled with soft feathers covers someone asleep in bed.
